title: Early Digital Shield and Parental Mental Health
summary: In the first two years of life, a child's brain grows at the fastest pace of their whole life, through real human interaction and sensory play. All the major medical organisations recommend a 'zero screens' policy: no screens, phones or baby-song channels at all before the age of two, to protect the child from delayed speech, scattered attention and weak eye contact. At the same time, the mother's mental health needs care: telling the passing 'baby blues' apart from postpartum depression, and the spouses sharing the load to prevent burnout and chronic exhaustion.
try_this: This week: agree as a couple to make the baby's room completely free of screens and digital distractions. Set a flexible schedule for sharing night-time care so the mother gets at least 4 hours of unbroken sleep to restore her mental and physical energy.
reflection_prompts: What natural alternatives (talking, singing, sensory toys) will you offer your child instead of playing videos?
How can we notice and deal with postnatal exhaustion together, as one team?
